turns.user: I'm starting a small vegetable garden on the back patio this spring, using six raised wooden beds that are each about one metre by two. The patio gets full sun in the morning and shade after three in the afternoon. I would like to grow tomatoes, beans, lettuce and a few herbs. Could you suggest which beds should hold which plants, so that the taller ones do not shade the rest?

Thanks. The soil I bought is a peat-free compost mixed with some garden loam, and it drains quite quickly. I am worried that the beds will dry out during the warm weeks in July, because I am often away from home for two or three days at a time. What is a simple watering setup that would keep everything alive without wasting a lot of water or needing power?

Let us talk about the tomatoes first. I have seeds for a cherry variety and a larger beefsteak type with no name on the packet. The packet says to start them indoors eight weeks before the last frost. If the last frost here is usually in the middle of April, when should I sow them, how deep should the seeds go, and how warm does the windowsill need to be for them to sprout?

I also want to keep a plain log of what I plant and when, so that next year I can see what worked and what did not. I was thinking of a simple spreadsheet with one row per sowing. Which columns would be worth recording from the start, and is there anything people often forget to write down that turns out to matter later in the season?

Something has been eating the young lettuce leaves overnight. There are small round holes in the leaves and a faint shiny trail along the wooden edge of the bed in the morning. I would rather not use pellets, because a hedgehog visits the patio most evenings. What are the gentler ways to protect the lettuce, and which of them tend to work best in practice?

Back to the watering plan for a moment. I found a rain barrel that holds two hundred litres and a long length of soaker hose. The barrel would sit on a stand about forty centimetres high next to the first bed. Is that enough height for the water to flow through the hose to all six beds, or will the far end of the row get almost nothing?

A friend down the road offered me some of her spare strawberry runners. I have room for one more container on the patio, a wide pot about forty centimetres across. How many runners would fit in a pot of that size, should they go in now or wait until the autumn, and do strawberries mind sharing the space with the tomatoes and the beans?

The beans are climbing faster than I expected, and some of them have already reached the top of the canes, which are about one metre eighty tall. Should I pinch out the growing tips at this point, or let them keep going and wind them back down along the canes? I would like more pods to pick rather than more leaves, and I do not want the plants to fall over.

A few of the lower tomato leaves have turned yellow with brown spots, starting at the edges and slowly moving inward. The upper leaves still look healthy and green, and the first trusses of flowers are opening. Is this something I should treat right away, or is it normal for older leaves at this stage, and should I remove the affected ones now or leave them?

Thank you for all of this. To finish, could you give me a short list of the jobs for the coming two weeks, in order of importance, covering the watering, the slugs, the tomatoes, the beans and the new strawberries? Please keep each job to one line, so that I can copy the whole list onto the small whiteboard that hangs by the back door.
